title: CinderBox ops runway and stability playback
summary: Quarterly ops review focused on usage runway, recent latency spikes during peak, and next-phase pilot for private deployment. Customer asked for security artifacts and an on-site performance demo of their checkout flow. Agreed pilot scope and timeline, and a short benchmark plan to validate latency targets under the 95th percentile. Action items: send SOC2 + SOC2 type II summary, schedule pilot ramp window, share benchmark spreadsheet, and set up a 4‑hour live run with customer traffic replay.
topics: dedicated vs hosted sizing and runway
next_steps: Sofia - send SOC2 summary + network diagram by 2025-10-24
Ben - share benchmark spreadsheet & test harness link by 2025-10-23
Jordan & Ben - align on traffic replay spec and schedule 4-hour run week of 2025-10-27
Maya - schedule follow-up pilot kickoff meeting for 2025-10-28

transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — we'll run 45-60 minutes. We want to cover usage runway, that latency spike last Thursday, and the proposed private pilot.
[00:18] Ethan (Head of ML): Yep, thanks Sofia. We had a few folks join, we'll probably drop in and out.
[00:25] Lena (VP Product): Hi all. High level — our Q4 launch needs the checkout inference at sub-120ms 95th, so timeline's tight.
[00:35] Ben (SE): Got it. We pulled the 95th P95 and P99 across last two weeks, and saw a tail increase during checkout surges. We'll share the raw traces after.
[00:46] Jordan (Infra): To call out, our infra had autoscale latencies too — some pods stuck in pending for ~30s, so that compounded request latency.
[00:55] Maya (CSM): I'll capture the ops notes and make sure next steps include a replay.
[01:02] Priya (Security): Quick intro from security — our main concerns are data residency and key management, and whether Redwood can support HSM-backed keys.
[01:14] Sofia (AE): Yes we support KMS integrations; HSM via our Private offering is possible. We'll include the KMS integration diagram in the packet.
[01:22] Ethan: Great. Can we start with the usage runway — essentially how much buffer we have before spend ramps? We hit a surprising token billline last month.
[01:33] Ben: Sure, high level: your daily token consumption doubled during the promo spikes. The main drivers were longer contexts and more candidate re-reranks. We recommended two levers — prefix caching for common prompts, and slightly more aggressive quantization for low-risk endpoints.
[01:47] Jordan: Could you explain quantization tradeoffs again? We tried a 4-bit variant and saw slight degradations on abstractive outputs.
[01:55] Ben: Yeah the 4-bit gave ~35% cost drop but some small coherence issues on long summaries. For checkout scoring (binary-ish), 4-bit looks safe; for long form product description, we keep 8-bit or mixed.
[02:10] Lena: So for the checkout path we can push aggressive optimization, everything else stays on higher fidelity. That helps our run rate.
[02:18] Sofia: Perfect — that matches our recommended model profiles. We'll add a recommended rollout plan per route.
[02:26] Ethan: About the latency spike: timeline and root cause?
[02:31] Ben: We looked — there was a burst of requests at the same time as a model rollout and a region failover. That combination hit cold KV cache and a bigger-than-usual batching window, so tail latency rose.
[02:44] Jordan: The failover was because our cluster scaled down aggressively at 2am and then couldn't spin up in time for morning traffic — autoscaler thresholds need tuning.
[02:53] Ben: Right, we suggested setting a floor on dedicated pools during business hours and enabling burst capacity for those windows. That reduces cold-starts, and keeps KV cache warm.
[03:05] Priya: From security side, the question is whether logs include PII. We need to ensure audit logs are redacted or access controlled.
[03:14] Sofia: Redwood audit logs can be configured to mask fields; with Private deployment we can ship logs to your SIEM and apply retention policies. We'll send sample log output.
[03:25] Lena: For the pilot we want to validate end-to-end — from SSO to key rotation to canary rollback. Can Redwood do canary A/B rollouts?
[03:35] Ben: Yes — our rollout tool supports canary percentages and automatic fallback to a previous model if latency or error thresholds breach. We can tie that to per-route thresholds and circuit-breakers.
[03:46] Ethan: Good. What's the proposed pilot scope?
[03:50] Sofia: We proposed a 4-week pilot: week 0 prep (networking, keys, small replay), week 1 traffic replay / baseline, week 2 live 5% traffic, week 3 ramp to 25% and run a 4-hour full-traffic stress test. Success: sub-120ms P95 and no increase in error-rate beyond 0.1%.
[04:11] Jordan: We can provide production snippets for replay but need auth tokens for the harness.
[04:17] Ben: We'll provide the harness and a spreadsheet with the test matrix — per-route batch sizes, kv-cache priming scripts, and expected throughput.
[04:25] Priya: Will you share SOC2 + penetration test summary? We need to pass internal review.
[04:30] Sofia: Yes — action item, I'll send a compliance packet that includes SOC2 attestation, network diagram, and high-level pen test summary. We can't attach full pen test results, but we can coordinate an NDA if you need more.
[04:45] Lena: Timeline wise, if we get the docs this week we can approve pilot the following Monday. That works with our launch.
[04:52] Maya: I'll schedule the kickoff for 10/28 and invite engineering owners.
[04:58] Ethan: A couple of technical clarifications — what kernel selection decisions do you make for long context models? Do you prefer fused attention kernels?
[05:07] Ben: We auto-select kernels based on sequence distribution and hardware; on Ampere we use fused attention for short sequences, and a different path for long seqs. There are heuristics exposed if you want to pin them.
[05:19] Jordan: Any chance of on-prem appliance? We have air-gap requirements for some retail partners.
[05:23] Sofia: We offer a Private on-prem package but it has a longer lead time. For immediate needs, VPC deployment with customer-controlled WAN is usually acceptable. For air-gapped we can scope though it pushes timelines ~8-12 weeks.
[05:38] Ethan: Ok noted. Let's finalize next steps.
[05:41] Sofia: Recap: Sofia sends compliance + network docs; Ben shares benchmark spreadsheet and replay harness; Jordan exports traffic snippet and tokens; Maya schedules kickoff. We'll run the 4-hour live replay week of 10/27.
[05:54] Lena: Thanks all. One last ask — can you put the pilot success criteria in a single doc we can follow?
[05:59] Maya: Yep, I'll own that doc and include dashboard links and alerts.
[06:04] Sofia: Great, we'll follow up with links. Thanks everyone.
[06:09] Speaker 3 (misc): [inaudible]
[06:12] Sofia: End call.
